prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a near-to-far gradient from the camera wearer's brightest lower torso (~0.2–0.3 m below the camera) and extended arms (~0.3–0.5 m in front) to a semi-circular art table (~0.4–0.9 m in front and below) and a dark background room (~1.5–3.0 m away). On the table within the wearer's arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m away, spaced ~0.1–0.3 m apart) sit a flat dog painting in front, a smartphone and pencil case to the left, a palette to the right, and two water jars plus a tall brush holder protruding upward near the back edge (~0.7–0.9 m), with a small rolling cart slightly lower to the bottom-left (~0.6–0.8 m). Across frames 1 to 3 the wearer looks straight down with their right forearm occluding the lower-right of the painting; in frame 4 the wearer's left hand enters at the bottom-left while a second person's hip and hand appear partly out of view at the far left (~1.2–1.5 m away); and in frame 5 the wearer turns their head up and left, shifting the table to the bottom-right and revealing the standing person ~1.2–1.6 m away to the upper-left (~0.5 m left of the table) facing and looking downward toward the camera wearer with bills held in their left hand within their own reach (~0.4 m from their torso, ~1.1 m from the wearer). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the 3D vertical relief of the protruding brushes, water jars, and standing person's silhouette from the cluttered background and flat tabletop artwork. However, the depth map is unreliable where the flat dog painting and reference photo show faint texture-induced depth artifacts, thin brush tips merge into a single jagged mass, and the lower table edge in frame 5 becomes overly saturated in brightness.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map outlines the spatial footprint of the scene's main surfaces and objects, placing the camera wearer ('person', ~0.2–0.5 m) at the bottom foreground, the tabletop ('dining table', ~0.4–0.9 m) spanning the middle, the dog painting ('book', ~0.4–0.6 m) centered on the table, a 'cup' (water jar, ~0.6–0.7 m) behind the painting, and a 'cell phone' (~0.5–0.6 m) to the left, all within the wearer's arm's reach and ~0.1–0.4 m from one another. Across frames 1 to 3, the wearer's right arm extends over the lower-right of the 'book' mask and occludes the dog's face on the canvas in frame 3; in frame 4, the wearer's left arm enters from the bottom-left to hold the bottom edge of the canvas while the table begins shifting right; and in frame 5, as the camera turns left, the table and 'book' move to the bottom-right and a standing 'person' mask appears at the upper-left (~1.2–1.6 m away, ~0.5 m left of the table), facing toward the wearer with their top of head and lower ankles partly cut off by the frame border. This map makes the exact 2D boundaries of the canvas, tabletop, and standing person immediately distinct from the surrounding floor and clutter, which visually blend together in the RGB strip. However, the segmentation is unreliable in several places: in frame 1 the 'book' mask bleeds leftward across the tabletop to absorb the reference photo, in frame 2 the wearer's torso is mislabeled as 'handbag', in frames 3–5 the pencil case and reference photo are misclassified as 'cell phone' and 'book', and in frame 3 the wearer's right arm is completely unsegmented (black) while the standing person's left edge in frame 4 is missed entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1 and 2, detects only the camera wearer's right hand (~0.4–0.5 m in front and below the camera) in frame 3, adds the wearer's left hand (~0.35–0.45 m away, ~0.2 m left of the right hand) in frame 4, and in frame 5 shows the wearer's left hand at the bottom alongside a full yellow body skeleton for the standing person at the upper-left (~1.2–1.6 m from the wearer and ~0.8–1.2 m from the wearer's hands). Where detected, the magenta hand skeletons sit within the wearer's immediate reach at the lower edge of the painting, while in frame 5 the standing person's yellow skeleton shows their shoulders, torso, and hips angled toward the bottom-right and their head keypoints tilted downward toward the camera wearer, with their left wrist extending forward to ~1.1 m from the wearer (within the standing person's own reach and ~0.6 m above and left of the table). Across the sequence, the pose map tracks the inward convergence of the wearer's two hands from frame 3 to frame 4 and the camera's leftward pan in frame 5 that brings the standing person's full body into view while the wearer's right hand becomes occluded or drops out at the bottom-right. Compared to RGB, the skeleton wireframes isolate exact joint centers, torso orientation, and finger articulations without visual distraction from clothing or background clutter. However, the map is highly unreliable where it completely misses the wearer's visible right hand and arm in frames 1, 2, and 5, fails to detect the wearer's torso throughout the strip, misses the partial person entering on the left in frame 4, and omits the detailed magenta finger keypoints on the standing person's hands in frame 5.
